speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the blisters on your forearm and the mouth ulcers first appeared, and have you noticed any fever, joint pain, or sensitivity to sunlight?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the blisters on your forearm occur in areas exposed to sunlight, and have you noticed any new skin lesions or mucosal involvement on other parts of your body? I also need to check if you have been taking any other new medications recently.

text: The blisters are indeed sun-exposed, and I see erosions in the mouth and vagina, but no other new skin lesions. The only recent medication change was stopping meloxicam two weeks ago and starting captopril.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, osteoarthritis. Social history: Has started hiking in the woods on weekends. No relevant travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to evaluate the blister for fragility. Please extend your arm so I can gently rub the edge of an intact blister on your forearm to see if the epidermis separates easily from the dermis, known as a positive Nikolsky sign.

speaker: Patient
text: No recent illnesses, denies fever, respiratory symptoms, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: I cannot perform a physical exam like the Nikolsky sign through this interface, so I will request diagnostic testing instead. REQUEST TEST: Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The immunofluorescence results showing intercellular IgG and C3 deposition, combined with your sun-exposed blisters and mucosal involvement, are classic for Pemphigus Vulgaris. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris
